campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is counted in promotions, not landings: a cycle that measured, trained or changed, judged on held-out data and moved main. While main trails the landings since its last promotion, rows that close the cycle rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a cycle that cannot finish (killed, withheld) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and promotion of main requires them on the commit it promotes; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

User-journey performance (owner, 2026-10-05). Optimize complete journeys, measured as action to usable result: submit to first visible answer, cold model selection to usable response, cancel to actual resource release, interrupted cycle to useful progress, with loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering kept apart. Start from the existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles of repeated reads, model loads, allocations and evidence reconstruction, and keep added instrumentation only when it explains a real elapsed-time gain. In the development loop one valid gate execution is shared by every compatible plan step and obligation, and validation and reuse are scoped by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated and embedded data, models, recipes, environment, subprocess effects); an unknown dependency keeps the broader coverage. A gain is judged against total maintenance cost (production code, tests, fixtures, instrumentation, gate work and upkeep): remove repeated processing through existing owners, and decline small gains that need disproportionate machinery. Prove with behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, never a new performance ratchet, selector or framework.

items.title: Hold each weak or surprising scorecard reading to a reference, a baseline and its own protocol before calling it the model's

budget.reason: A new kind of held-out suite, for a model that remembers a document in notes it writes to itself: its cases, its report and its builder, beside the measure in the model's package; the owner asked on 2026-10-07 for the model double-check recommendation to be planned

steps.title: Draw the infographics at SenseNova's own size and steps, and record what the judge reads in them
steps.rationale: The step before this one builds the measure: twenty briefs, each an infographic asked to hold a title, three lines with a figure and a line of small print, and for each text a question that offers it among three near it. This step is the reading. Build evaluate at the commit that holds the measure; draw the twenty at 2048 by 2048, 50 steps, guidance 4, timestep shift 3, against a copy of the store, about two minutes a picture; look at four of the pictures by eye; judge them on the copy first, where a reading at the ceiling or at chance says the measure tells nothing, then on the real store; and say on the scorecard which of SenseNova's readings is of its use. The judge's own reading of text is part of what is measured: say what it reads on a picture whose text is known to be right, if one can be made without a download. Serves: measure and find the gap. Disappears: a reading beside the point. Evidence: the reading on the scorecard, and the four pictures looked at. Batch: device.

steps.title: Edit the clips as told, look at eight, and record what the judge finds changed and kept
steps.rationale: The step before this one builds the measure: a clip whose caption names one worn thing by a colour, the instruction to change that colour and nothing else, and one question of four captions that tells the change and the rest apart. This step is the reading. Build evaluate at the commit that holds the measure; edit 64 clips with -render-edits -one-thing against a copy of the store, at the editor's own size, about 75 seconds a clip; look at eight edited clips beside their sources by eye, and say what the editor did; judge on the copy first, where a reading at the ceiling or at chance says the measure tells nothing, then on the real store; tally the wrong answers by kind, unchanged or scene lost. Serves: measure and find the gap. Disappears: a reading beside the point. Evidence: the reading on the scorecard, the tally, and the eight clips looked at. Batch: device.

steps.title: Let an edit request carry its source clip without loss
steps.rationale:
The served edit agrees with the earlier implementation's clip at about 28 dB over 8-pixel squares when its source arrives as a GIF, smoothed, and at 41 dB when the runtime is given the frames the reference fed. What is left is the format the source arrives in: a GIF keeps 256 colours a frame, and the smoothing that removes its grain also removes detail the editor would have kept. Smoothing is a repair of a lossy source, not a way to carry one.

The step gives an edit request a way to carry its source without loss, as frames or as the video file the evaluation already decodes, keeps the GIF form with its smoothing for requests that send one, and raises the served comparison's bound to what the lossless form reaches. The held-out edit suite is rendered from lossless sources and judged again if the comparison moves by more than its tolerance.

Serves: generate. Disappears: a known loss in the editor's input. Evidence: the device test at its new bound, and the edit reading. Batch: device.

items.title: Count a word error rate over a reference and a transcript written one way, as the recognizers' own evaluations do

budget.reason: A port of the English normalizer that speech recognizers' evaluations count word errors with, about 480 lines of Python of which the reader of spelled-out numbers is the bulk, with its tables embedded as that code builds them; the suite field that names it and the builders that write it. A step of the owner's double-check of the scorecard: hold a reading to its own protocol

steps.title: Score the E4B projector's transcription again, counted the recognizers' way
steps.rationale: The projector's 32 held-out transcripts cannot be counted again from the store as the two recognizers' were (commit of word-error-forms/rescore): a projected transcription run is bound to the plan it ran under, which names the prompt and the token budget it decoded with, and a suite counted another way is another plan, so the evaluator refuses the stored runs (transcription run authority differs). Its reading therefore stays 0.02567, counted over the words as written, and the scorecard says so beside the two recognizers counted the other way; with the normalizer's own code the stored transcripts read 15 words wrong of 787, 0.019. To move the reading: recover the suite from the store (the plan's case profile of report evaluation:sha256:69f0bfa7cf at sequence 7989), name whisper-english in it, rebuild the resource manifest's inputs from the LibriSpeech test parquet rows the suite names, and run evaluate -transcription-resource-manifest for gemma-4-E4B-it on the device, on a copy of the store first. Done when the scorecard's section on how word error rates were counted names no reading counted as written.

items.title: Compare the path an image-gen request takes with a reference output for each model it is scored on

budget.reason: The comparison of each served image generator's request path with the fixed-seed picture its reference kept, as the served edit path is compared; a step of the owner's double-check of the scorecard, named for the gap the scorecard files for it

steps.title: Hold each served image generator's request path to the picture its reference kept
steps.rationale:
LiveEdit's runtime agreed with the earlier implementation's latent and clip while the path a request takes around it read its source in the wrong range, wrote its frames in the wrong range, projected its prompt with the wrong weights and drew its clips in a palette the editor read as content. Krea-2-Turbo and SenseNova-U1 have comparisons of their runtimes; for neither is the path from a prompt to the served picture held to a reference. Their judged readings, 0.9301 and 0.5157 on 415 cases, do not excuse them: a judge asked which caption fits can pass a washed picture.

For each generator whose reference kept a fixed-seed picture and its settings, the step sends the same prompt, seed and settings as a served request and compares the picture with the kept one, square by square and in its dark and bright levels, as the edit test does, with a tolerance taken from the reference's own variation, and names the test in the scorecard's path comparisons. Where the reference kept none, it records the deferral and what would reopen it. A difference is a fault in the path: it is fixed and the generator is scored again. SimpleDiffusion has no held-out reading and so no gap here; its comparison with its upstream code, run twice for a tolerance, is done with these if its reference can be run.

Serves: measure and find the gap. Disappears: nothing. Evidence: the device tests, and the gap closing. Batch: device.

items.title: Compare the path a video-gen request takes with a reference output for each model it is scored on

budget.reason: The comparison of the served video generator's request path with the fixed-seed clip its reference kept, as the served edit path is compared; a step of the owner's double-check of the scorecard, named for the gap the scorecard files for it

steps.title: Hold Wan2.1's served request path to the clip its reference kept
steps.rationale:
LiveEdit's video-gen reading is compared: a device test holds the clip a served edit request returns to the clip the earlier implementation drew. Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B's is not. Its runtime has a comparison with the earlier implementation; the path from a prompt to the served clip, the text context, the sampler settings and the clip's encoding, is what LiveEdit's four faults were in, and Wan2.1 shares the text encoder and the clip encoder with it. Its judged reading of 0.9141 does not excuse it: a judge asked which caption fits can pass a washed clip.

The step sends the prompt, seed and settings of a clip the reference tree kept as a served request and compares the result with the kept clip, square by square and in its dark and bright levels, with a tolerance taken from the reference's own variation; it names the test in the scorecard's path comparisons. A difference is a fault in the path: it is fixed and the generator is scored again.

Serves: measure and find the gap. Disappears: nothing. Evidence: the device test, and the gap closing. Batch: device.

items.title: Compare the path an inference request takes with a reference output for each model it is scored on

budget.reason: For each of the eleven text models the scorecard reads, the test that compares what a served request returns with a reference output, named where it exists and written where the reference is on this machine, or a recorded deferral; and, since there was no way to see what a model is given without loading it, a reader of prompts that needs no model: a type in the runner's package, the one function that says what the chat-template protocol asks, and a mode of evaluate that prints it. A step of the owner's double-check of the scorecard, named for the gap the scorecard files for it

steps.title: Give Qwen2.5-0.5B its own chat template and score it again
steps.rationale:
Finding e683b1e7: the scored file of Qwen2.5-0.5B was converted before the converter carried a chat template, so its chat-template questions are asked in overgo's built-in ChatML with no system turn, where the model's own template opens with one. Its reading, 0.0786 on MMLU-Pro, is below the 0.1109 of a constant answer. Convert the model again so the file carries its template, register it, score store/mmlu-pro under the chat-template protocol on the device, and remove its entry from the test's known faults, which fails once the tokens match. Whether the reading moves is not known; say what it does.

Measured on 2026-10-08 before the file is replaced, with tmp/system_turn_probe.go on the scored file and 600 of the suite's questions taken evenly: asked as the evaluation asks now the model has 46 right, 0.077, and the evaluation reads no letter in 277 of its 600 answers; with the system turn its own template opens with put before the question, which makes the text token for token what the template gives, it has 74 right, 0.123, and no letter in 161. The answer differs on 300 of the 600. So the missing turn costs this model about five points and takes its reading from below a constant answer's 0.111 to beside it. The model is the base model and not an instruct one: either way it often writes on past its letter or writes none, which is the model and not the path. A file converted today (overgo_data/scratch/qwen25-template/Qwen2.5-0.5B-f16.gguf, 2560 bytes longer than the scored one) is given the model's own tokens on all 24 of the fixture's cases. The scored file sits under adaptive_new's checkpoints, a tree this lane does not write to, so the new file goes under overgo_data and the step says which file the scorecard's row is then read from.

steps.title: Give Unlimited-OCR the splitting rule of its own tokenizer, or retire its plain-text reading
steps.rationale:
Finding 34979bff: the scored file of Unlimited-OCR names the pre-tokenizer of an earlier DeepSeek tokenizer, and the model's tokenizer.json holds a later rule that joins a mark with the line break after it; overgo has no such rule. The model's own short prompts tokenize the same either way, so its use is untouched; its MMLU-Pro reading, already marked as not a measure of what the model is for, was asked with every line's end tokenized otherwise. Adding the rule changes internal/tokenizer, which moves the pinned inference surface and costs a device pass; the owner may prefer to retire the plain-text reading of an OCR model instead. Decide with the cost in hand, then do one or the other and remove the entry from the test's known faults.

Decided and half done on 2026-10-08 (step ocr-rule): the rule is added and not the reading retired. overgo now has DeepSeek-V3's three splits as the rule deepseek-v3, held to 12467 pieces the model's own tokenizer cuts, and its converter names that sequence. The checkpoint converted by overgo is at overgo_data/models/Unlimited-OCR-bf16/ (Unlimited-OCR-bf16.gguf and Unlimited-OCR-mmproj-bf16.gguf): every tensor holds the same numbers as the scored files', which sit under adaptive_new's checkpoints, a tree this lane does not write to. 144 of the language file's 155 tensors and 444 of the projector's 476 are the same bytes; the other 11, each block's router, and 32, the projector's position tables and convolutions, are stored as bf16 by overgo's converter where the scored files hold them as f32, and expand to the same f32 values. The metadata differs in more than the rule's name: overgo's file carries no chat template, the checkpoint shipping none, where the scored file carries one that joins the messages' contents; it lacks the scored file's sliding-window and expert-group keys and its descriptive ones, and has key and value lengths, an expert weights scale and a rope base the scored file lacks. So the two are not known to serve alike until the device says so. The new file is given the model's own tokens on all 24 of the reading's questions (fixtures/prompt_ids/Unlimited-OCR.json). What is left is the device's: register the new file as the first was (commit d6031e627: verified on exact cases minted from the runtime, activated, tied to its checkpoint directory, with its smoke oracle), hold what it serves for a document picture to what the scored file serves, the absent chat template being the first thing to look at, score store/mmlu-pro under raw completion with it, let the scorecard's row read it, say what the reading does, then remove fixtures/prompt_ids/Unlimited-OCR-bf16.json and its entry among the test's known faults.

steps.title: Name, write or defer the comparison of each text model's served path with a reference output
steps.rationale:
Eleven text models are scored on inference: Bonsai-27B-Q1_0, Carbon-500M, MiniCPM5-1B, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, Unlimited-OCR, gemma-4-E4B-it and the two builds of gemma-4-12B-it-fp8. For none does the scorecard name a test that compares what a served request returns with a reference output. That is not to say none exists: the recommendation counted many tests that name an oracle or a parity, and the benchmark report already sets a published figure, and for some models a run of the Hugging Face implementation on the same weights, beside each suite. What has not been done is to say, model by model, which test holds the served path, the prompt as a request renders it, the tokens, the sampler and the decoded text, and not only the forward pass, to a reference.

The step goes through the eleven. For each it names the test that makes that comparison where one exists; writes it where the reference output is on this machine, which for the two quantized builds is the unquantized original and for the fp8 gemma its bf16 one; and otherwise records why no comparison is made and what would reopen it, a deferral shown on the scorecard as a deferral and not as a pass. A comparison that needs a download becomes an owner decision. MiniCPM5's thinking switch and its tool call, its stated strength, are compared on and off where its reference can be run.

Done on 2026-10-08 toward this step, and what is left of it. Reference answers are written on the host and wait on the device, which a judging run holds most of: gemma-4-E4B's to its 24 questions and its ten conversations; and for both builds of gemma-4-12B, from the unquantized original (overgo_data/models/gemma-4-12B-it) with each of its 144 fp8 tensors put in place as fp8 value times its row's weight_scale, a rule the script checks against the original (mean relative distance 0.0225, the 485 tensors the two share unquantized bit-equal). They are under overgo_data/scratch/answer-reference; copy each into fixtures/answer_log_probabilities, run cmd/evaluate TestModelsAnswerAsTransformersDoes with the device free, and name the test for gemma-4-12B-it-fp8, the bf16 build, whose reading is still filed. The fp8 values are three bits of mantissa, so the tolerance may not be the half-precision one: measure, and say what it is. Then the deferrals: Bonsai-27B, Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B are GGUF files with no original on this machine, and a reference for them is a build of llama.cpp or a download, which is the owner's to approve.

Serves: measure and find the gap. Disappears: nothing. Evidence: the tests and the recorded deferrals, and the gap closing. Batch: device.

items.title: Compare the path a reconstruction request takes with a reference output for each model it is scored on

budget.reason: The comparison of each autoencoder's served reconstruction with its reference's on the same picture, or a recorded deferral; a step of the owner's double-check of the scorecard, named for the gap the scorecard files for it

steps.title: Hold the three autoencoders' served reconstructions to their references'
steps.rationale:
Wan2.1's video autoencoder reads 41.37 dB on 128 frames, the representation autoencoder 20.53 dB on 128 pictures, and the encoder bridged into it 18.16 dB. A reconstruction measure compares a model's output with its own input, so a path that loses detail reads as a model that loses detail. The step names, for each, the test that compares the served latent or the served reconstruction with the reference implementation's on the same picture, writes it where the reference is on this machine, or records the deferral.

Serves: measure and find the gap. Disappears: nothing. Evidence: the tests or the recorded deferrals, and the gap closing. Batch: device.

items.title: Measure whether past-experiment evidence improves the proposer's candidates

budget.reason: The comparison of a proposer with and without the past experiments the reader of experiment-evidence returns; split from that row so the owner's double-check of the scorecard's readings runs before it, the comparison not having started

steps.title: Measure whether that evidence improves the proposer's candidates
steps.rationale:
Three arms with the same proposer and the same budget: no evidence, the store's current retrieval, and the cut-off reader of the step before. The exact bytes each arm read are recorded. Judged by the held-out objective of the proposer's row; no benefit is a valid outcome and closes the step. A learned encoder of experiment paths is not planned unless the plain reader measurably falls short.

Serves: judge on held-out data. Disappears: nothing. Evidence: the held-out score of each arm. Batch: device.

items.title: Close the campaign once every branch is accounted for

steps.title: Verify the final release surface and publish campaign closure
steps.verify: go run ./cmd/gate -preflight && go run ./cmd/benchmark-report -check && go run ./cmd/validate -claims
steps.rationale: Run final host, race, device, browser and release checks once, reusing only proven-independent evidence. Resolve high-priority findings; record dispositions and reopen triggers for deferred capability. Reconcile census, baseline and reports at the closing commit and bind the census. The operator stop stays until the operator resumes.

decisions.question: Download the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it? The 12B FP8 twins score 0.5-1.2 nats per token worse than E4B on the guard corpus while overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers reference, so the third-party quant is the suspect.
options: Download it
Keep only the FP8 twins and record the gap

decisions.question: The capability census changed from 209 recorded identities to 220 live ones. Record a disposition that accepts the live census as the new denominator?
options: Review the 11 new identities, then accept
Accept the live census as it stands
decisions.recommendation: Review the 11 new identities, then accept
decisions.answer: Review the 11 new identities, then accept

decisions.question: Four test groups need references only the Python originals produce: the Fractale leadership tests, Krea, Pocket TTS and the Qwen3.5 projector fixture. What happens to them?
options: Delete those a running test covers, keep the rest waiting
Allow one Python run to produce the references
Keep all waiting
decisions.recommendation: Delete those a running test covers, keep the rest waiting
decisions.answer: Allow one Python run to produce the references

decisions.question: When validate-currency is otherwise ready, should the Qwen3.5-9B hybrid training proof (22m05 a cycle, the same cmd/train route and code as the blocking 4B proof) move to the background, so promotion stops waiting on every training proof? Background saves about 22 min a cycle; the 4B proof still guards the route.
options: background
blocking

decisions.question: The scorecard's serving cells (first-output, throughput, load-time, peak-device-memory) aggregate every attempt a recipe ever made: medians over all time, total tokens over total decode time, the highest peak ever. A landed improvement shows only as old samples are outnumbered and a peak never falls. Since delete-selection each cycle measures every serving cell once at the measured commit. Should those cells read the newest successful measured attempt instead, accepting one sample's timing noise in each cycle's moved list?
options: newest measured attempt
all-time aggregates
median of the newest few attempts

decisions.question: Held-out quality is unscored for forecast, image-embedding, image-gen, seq2seq, tabular and vqa because each needs a held-out set the store lacks. Answering authorizes exactly these downloads into the datasets root, each to be verified by hash once fetched: ETTh1 (github.com/zhouhaoyi/ETDataset, 2.6 MB, forecast); BFCL v3 simple (gorilla-llm/Berkeley-Function-Calling-Leaderboard, 0.3 MB, seq2seq); BeyondArena credit-g (TabArena/BeyondArena, 0.2 MB, tabular); TIFA v1.0 (github.com/Yushi-Hu/tifa, 10 MB, image-gen); A-OKVQA validation (HuggingFaceM4/A-OKVQA, 60 MB, vqa); Imagenette 160 px (fast.ai imagenette2-160, 100 MB, image-embedding). About 173 MB in all. The other five unscored rows (generation, projection, speech, training, video-gen) use sets already on disk and are not blocked.
options: Download all six (about 173 MB)
Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)
Download none and score only what is on disk
decisions.answer: Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)

decisions.question: The remaining models under adaptive_new/models (Wan, the Gemma configs and others) are read by tests through variables that point outside the repository, which cost environment-dependent skips. May they be copied into overgo_data/models, one model at a time, each copy verified (hash, servable identity, baseline lookup, bounded inference) before its locator switches, with the originals left in place and adaptive_new never written to?
options: Copy one at a time, verified, originals kept
Leave adaptive_new as the models' home
decisions.recommendation: Copy one at a time, verified, originals kept
decisions.answer: Copy one at a time, verified, originals kept

decisions.question: Held-out quality is unscored for generation (Fractale-350M-base) because the held-out text the proposal names, the WikiText-2 test split (Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-2-raw-v1, 0.7 MB), is not on disk: only wikitext2_train.txt is, which a model may have trained on. Answering authorizes exactly this one download into the datasets root.
options: Download the WikiText-2 test split (about 0.7 MB)
Score generation on a held-out membership of the on-disk training articles instead
Download nothing and leave generation unscored

decisions.answer: Download the WikiText-2 test split (about 0.7 MB)

decisions.question: gemma-4-12B-it-fp8 (the non-native file) is slower, heavier and slower to load than the native file at equal held-out quality (31.1 tok/s, 31.1 s load, 22.5 GiB against 41.5 tok/s, 22.6 s, 14.7 GiB; 0.4919 against 0.4926; the native file now decodes at 45 tok/s and loads in 7.5 s). Does it still serve anything that justifies the device time of its eight cycle cells and any optimization?
options: Keep it registered and measured, spend no optimization time on it
Retire it from the cycle and keep the file
Delete the file
decisions.recommendation: Keep it registered and measured, spend no optimization time on it
decisions.answer: Keep it registered and measured, spend no optimization time on it

decisions.question: Editing a pinned media runtime path (go.mod, kernels, internal/cuda, tensor, devicemath and the rest of docs/image_video_merged.json's runtime paths) needs a reviewed delta: a device receipt, a delta entry, and the registry's identity pinned in a test, built by hand twice on 2026-10-04 and again for every kernel row ahead (e4b-decode-graph, decode-small-kernels). It exists so media evidence acquired at the pinned runtime stays valid across an output-neutral edit. Since the cycle re-acquires every media cell at the commit it promotes, and its models lane runs the media acceptance tests against the frozen references, the evidence that gate protects is re-proved every cycle: it is the same per-cell currency check validate-currency deleted. Retire the registry, its pin and the gate-time check (about 600 lines of test code, the registry JSON and the landing's pinned-path rule), or keep it and build a one-command tool for it (row media-delta-command)?
options: Retire the pin, the registry and the gate-time check; the cycle's media acceptance holds the contract
Keep the pin and build the one-command delta tool (media-delta-command)

decisions.question: Speech, image-gen and video-gen quality cannot be scored by the model alone: pocket-tts outputs audio, the image generators pictures, Wan2.1 and Un-0 clips. Each proposal scores the output by a second local model: a speech recognizer for round-trip word error rate, a vision-language model for TIFA questions and for matching a clip to its caption. evaluate has no suite in which a generator's output is judged by another model, and a record must name both the generator's recipe, which the scorecard reads, and the judge's identity, which the score depends on. One judged-generation suite kind (the projection session already shows a video to Qwen3.8-27B) would serve all three rows and their eight models, with a new session for each judge modality.
options: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
Score speech by its recognizer round trip only, and leave image-gen and video-gen unscored
Leave all three unscored
decisions.recommendation: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
decisions.answer: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen

decisions.question: Held-out quality of training is scored for a recipe only by a train -objective session, which publishes a held-out verdict. Qwen2.5-0.5B trains through that route and now has its verdict (a token-prediction objective over a held-out third of the WikiText-2 articles). The other six training recipes belong to routes that prove the route rather than score text: Qwen3.5-4B and 9B hybrid-stack (a bounded observed full-stack run whose evidence is that loss descends), Wan2.1 and LiveEdit dit, Hy-Embodied mot. None of those routes holds out data or scores a model, and a token-prediction objective does not fit a diffusion or a mixture-of-transformers model. Scoring them means giving each route a held-out objective of its own (days of work each, and a 20-step proof run's held-out value says little). Which do you want?
options: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
Give each proof route a held-out objective and score its recipe
Leave the proof-route recipes unscored
decisions.recommendation: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
decisions.answer: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route

decisions.question: adaptive_new/models holds about 430 GB in 20 model directories (Krea-2-Turbo 116 GB, SenseNova-U1 66, bonzai 40, Wan2.1 33, LiveEdit 32, gemma-4-E4B 30, gemma-4-12B-fp8 29, Hy-Embodied 24, Qwen3.5-4B 18, Unlimited-OCR 13, pocket-tts 9, Qwen3.5-9B 9, then eight under 5 GB), and C: has 536 GB free at 86% full. The answer to adaptive-new-model-copies kept every original, so copying all of them leaves about 100 GB free. Which models should move into overgo_data/models now?
options: Copy the models under 10 GB now, and decide the large ones separately
Copy every model, originals kept (leaves about 100 GB free)
Copy the models under 10 GB now and leave the large ones where they are, their test variables kept
Copy the large ones too, then delete the originals after each verified copy
decisions.recommendation: Copy the models under 10 GB now, and decide the large ones separately
decisions.answer: Copy the models under 10 GB now, and decide the large ones separately

decisions.question: The ten large models under adaptive_new/models are about 204 GB of working files (their directories hold as much again in git LFS caches), adaptive_new/checkpoints is a further 211 GB and is overgo's configured checkpoints root, and C: has about 495 GB free. Copying all of it while the originals stay does not fit. How should the large models and the checkpoints root leave adaptive_new?
options: Leave them where they are for now, found through local-models.json, and take the hard-coded paths out of the tests
Move them: rename the large model directories and the checkpoints root into overgo_data (same volume, no disk cost, no copy time); this changes adaptive_new, so it needs the owner's word
Copy the large models' working files (about 204 GB, originals kept, leaves about 290 GB free) and leave the checkpoints root in adaptive_new
decisions.recommendation: Leave them where they are for now, found through local-models.json, and take the hard-coded paths out of the tests
decisions.answer: Leave them where they are for now, found through local-models.json, and take the hard-coded paths out of the tests

decisions.question: The owner told master on 2026-10-07 to take over the VAE lane and plan it as master sees fit. The lane's own plan is 32 steps, none started, behind about 3000 lines of contracts with no caller. What shape does the work take on master?
options: Five measured rows on master, each lane file ported with its first caller, optional branches unplanned until a proposer is kept
Merge the lane's contracts whole and follow its 32-step plan in order
Keep only the installed-autoencoder capability and its held-out measure, and retire the rest of the campaign
decisions.recommendation: Five measured rows on master, each lane file ported with its first caller, optional branches unplanned until a proposer is kept
